model.name: Access Contract / Consent
model.purpose: Represent a durable, machine-readable permission instrument that an owner (grantor) issues to a reader (grantee): who may read which objects, in which action and purpose, under which constraints and duties, on what evidence of consent or other assent, until when, and how the grant is verified, amended, withdrawn and proven.
model.scope_statement: This mixin models the agreement that authorises a read across an ownership boundary. It is not a property of the data object and not a property of the reader. It records parties, grant terms, scope, constraints, obligations, consent evidence and lifecycle so that other catalogue models can defer to a live instrument whenever data is disclosed. Semantics are format-neutral: JSON, YAML, tokens, receipts and API messages are projections. The mixin specialises a general contract for read permission and aligns, without claiming conformance, to ODRL Agreements, ISO/IEC TS 27560 consent records and receipts, ISO/IEC 29184 notice-and-consent controls, HL7 FHIR Consent privacy directives, W3C DPV consent records, Kantara Consent Receipt 1.1, and Kantara UMA 2.0 grant exercise.
in_scope: Identity, classification and version of an access-contract instrument, including Offer versus Agreement versus generic Set, and privacy-consent versus usage-licence flavours.
Parties and functional roles: grantor/assigner, grantee/assignee, subject/PII principal, manager, controller/enforcer, requesting party, and party collections with refinements.
Grant terms: permitted, prohibited and obligatory actions, purpose statements, legal-basis declaration when the grant is privacy consent, and default permit or deny.

Scope selection: target assets or registry objects, data-instance meaning, resource or document class, security labels, nested exception provisions, and references to disclosure-shape policies owned by a sibling model.
Constraints on a rule: temporal windows, spatial or jurisdiction limits, count/frequency, media/refinement, and logical combinations of constraints.
Grantee duties and remedies: no onward sharing, retention and erasure, payment or notice duties, and consequences of infringement.
Human consent expression: indication method, indication time, channel, language, consent type (expressed, explicit, informed), notice reference, and evidence artefacts.
Capacity to consent or to grant: self, holder of parental responsibility, guardian, or delegate whose authority is resolved in the ownership/delegation sibling.
Consent record versus consent receipt, demonstration that consent was obtained, and portable copies returned to the grantor or PII principal.
Lifecycle states and events: notice shown, requested, given, refused, reaffirmed, amended, withdrawn, expired, superseded, invalidated, and entered-in-error.
Operating functions: verify that a specific read is covered, issue or introspect an entitlement token, propagate revocation, and evidence discharge of post-termination duties.
Provenance of consent and grant events, verification/re-validation of the grantor decision, and quality flags that a stored record is not by itself proof of legal validity.
out_of_scope: Ownership, title, guardianship and delegation authority themselves; those resolve in the ownership sibling. A grant from a party who is not the holder or an authorised delegate is void, but this mixin does not store title.
Disclosure shape, projection, redaction and field-level transformation policies; scope clauses point at those policies rather than describing shapes.
Access audit logs of each exercise, grant or revocation; this mixin emits events that the audit sibling records.
Enforcement cases, sanctions and incident handling when a read is out of scope or a duty is breached; those belong to the enforcement sibling.
Authentication, identity proofing and credential issuance for parties.
Human-facing privacy-notice user experience, layering, accessibility presentation and cookie-banner UX except as a referenced notice artefact required for informedness.
Medical treatment consent, advance directives and research-protocol participation as clinical acts; FHIR models those uses, but this mixin covers only the information-access (privacy/read) directive.

Lawful bases other than consent or contractual permission to read, including legitimate interest, legal obligation, vital interest, public task and official authority, except as a classification that this instrument is not a consent grant.
Policy-evaluation engines, XACML encoding, OAuth/UMA wire protocol, token format and storage engines; UMA is an alignment for exercise, not the contract semantics.
The underlying personal data, research datasets or content assets being read.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Permission is an agreement, not an attribute
boundary_notes.distinction: ODRL treats Policy as a first-class object relating Party, Action and Asset. FHIR Consent is a first-class resource with grantor, grantee, period and provisions. ISO/IEC TS 27560 treats the consent record as its own information structure. This mixin therefore remains a separate catalogue entry rather than a flag on data or on a reader.

An ODRL Agreement can grant use of any Asset between any Parties, including organisations and non-personal content. GDPR consent is a legal basis that only a natural person (or a person acting for a child) can give for processing of personal data. Implementations MUST distinguish a usage/access licence from a privacy-consent grant; the same instrument template may carry both only when the grantor is the PII principal and the asset is personal data.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Authority to grant is not stored here
boundary_notes.distinction: Grantor capacity that depends on ownership, parental responsibility or delegation is resolved against the ownership sibling. This mixin records which capacity was claimed and the reference to the authority record, not the authority itself.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Shape of disclosure is not stored here
boundary_notes.distinction: FHIR provisions and ODRL target refinements select which objects and actions are in scope. The projection or redaction shape of a permitted read is a sibling disclosure-scope policy referenced from a scope clause.

ISO/IEC 29184 governs how a notice is presented and how consent is asked. ISO/IEC TS 27560 and this mixin record that a notice was in force and link to it. Matching a layered UI to a record is out of scope.

Kantara UMA 2.0 issues requesting-party tokens from policy conditions, but does not define those conditions. This mixin is the condition content; UMA, OAuth and XACML are interchangeable exercise projections.

GDPR does not cover legal persons or, by default, deceased persons. ODRL and FHIR still allow organisational grantors and related-person actors. Region-specific succession, estate and corporate-authority rules are gaps unless supplied by a jurisdictional profile.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: Normative information model for Policy, Set, Offer, Agreement, Permission, Prohibition, Duty, Asset, Party, Constraint, conflict strategy and rule evaluation.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation)
sources.relevance: Articles 4(11), 6(1)(a), 7, 8, 9(2)(a), 13-14, 17 and Recitals 32, 33, 38, 42, 43, 65 define consent qualities, demonstration, withdrawal, children, special-category explicit consent and erasure after withdrawal.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR R5 Resource Consent
sources.relevance: Computable privacy consent directive: identifier, status, grantor, grantee, manager, controller, period, decision permit/deny, nested provisions, purpose, data meaning, verification, source attachments and policyBasis including ODRL.

sources.title: ISO/IEC TS 27560:2023 Privacy technologies - Consent record information structure
sources.relevance: Interoperable consent record and consent receipt information structure; lifecycle management of recorded consent; no exchange protocol. Confirmed current; successor ISO/IEC CD 27560.2 under development.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 29184:2020 Information technology - Online privacy notices and consent
sources.relevance: Controls for notice content/structure and for obtaining consent that is fair, demonstrable, transparent, unambiguous and revocable. This mixin references notices; it does not implement notice UX.

sources.title: Consent Records and Receipts as per ISO/IEC TS 27560:2023 using DPV
sources.organization: W3C Data Privacy Vocabularies and Controls Community Group
sources.relevance: Authoritative field mapping among ISO 27560, GDPR and DPV; consent lifecycle states; record versus receipt; documents the Kantara receipt-direction conflict.

sources.title: User-Managed Access (UMA) 2.0 Grant for OAuth 2.0 Authorization
sources.relevance: Party-to-party asynchronous authorization, permission tickets, requesting-party tokens, claims gathering, token revocation via RFC 7009, and explicit statement that policy-condition content is out of band.

sources.title: Kantara Initiative Consent Receipt Specification v1.1.0
sources.relevance: Human-readable and JSON consent receipt: consentReceiptID, timestamp, collection method, PII principal, PII controllers, policy URL, purposes, consent type, PII categories, termination, third-party disclosure. Cited by ISO 27560 as a source; field-level examples also published in community JSON profiles.

bundles.name: Agreement instrument
bundles.description: The access contract as a first-class Policy or Consent Directive: identity, parties, permissions, purpose, scope, constraints and duties, independent of how consent was captured.
bundles.rationale: ODRL Policy, FHIR Consent and ISO/IEC TS 27560 records each treat the instrument as a first-class object, so its identity, parties, deontic terms, scope and constraints are grouped independently of how assent was captured.

layers.name: Identity and classification
layers.description: Identify the instrument, its type, version, regulatory basis and the policy language or profile it uses.

findings.name: Instrument identity
findings.description: An access contract MUST have a unique identifier. ODRL requires Policy.uid as an IRI. ISO/IEC TS 27560 requires a record identifier and a schema_version, and a distinct receipt identifier when a receipt is issued. FHIR Consent.identifier is a business identifier for a copy of the statement and is not the FHIR resource id. A calendar date is not an identifier. When the adopting Dimension masters the record, it assigns a UUID or ULID only after master-system and IRI identifiers are absent.

questions.text: What is the canonical identifier of this access contract, in which scheme, and which mastering system assigned it?
Which information-model profile and schema version interpret the terms of this instrument?
Is this instance the master record, a FHIR copy identifier, or a receipt that only references the record?

data_elements.name: access_contract_id
data_elements.description: Canonical instrument identifier. Prefer mastering-system id or ODRL uid IRI.

data_elements.name: id_scheme
data_elements.description: Scheme: odrl-uid, iso27560-record-id, fhir-identifier, dimension-ulid.

data_elements.name: schema_profile_uri
data_elements.description: ODRL profile, DPV-27560 profile, FHIR version, or Dimension profile IRI.

data_elements.name: instrument_version
data_elements.description: Version of this instrument, distinct from schema version.

data_elements.name: supersedes_contract_id
data_elements.description: Prior instrument this version replaces.

artifacts.name: Instrument header record
artifacts.description: Stable identity envelope: identifiers, schema/profile, version, language, jurisdiction, created and updated observation times.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by access_contract_id under the mastering-system-first identifier priority; instrument_version distinguishes successive headers.

findings.name: Instrument classification
findings.description: The same mixin covers several disjoint subtypes that MUST be classified rather than conflated: ODRL Set (generic rules), Offer (assigner offers, does not grant), Agreement (assigner has granted to assignee); FHIR privacy consent directive versus treatment or research-participation consent; ISO 27560 consent record (privacy processing) versus a non-personal usage licence. FHIR decision is permit or deny as the default, with nested provisions as exceptions. ODRL Policy may declare a conflict strategy (perm, prohibit, invalid). Regulatory basis and category support indexing but do not themselves grant access.

questions.text: Is this instrument an Offer, an Agreement already granted, a FHIR draft, or a mere Set of rules?
Does this grant authorise processing of personal data on a consent legal basis, or only usage of a non-personal asset?
If a requested read matches no provision, is the default permit, deny, or invalid-by-conflict?

data_elements.name: policy_subclass
data_elements.description: set | offer | agreement | fhir-consent | iso27560-record.

data_elements.name: grant_flavour
data_elements.description: privacy-consent | usage-licence | mixed-only-if-principal-is-grantor.

data_elements.name: default_decision
data_elements.description: permit | deny. FHIR Consent.decision; ODRL implies only stated permissions.

data_elements.name: conflict_strategy
data_elements.description: ODRL perm | prohibit | invalid.

data_elements.name: category_codes
data_elements.description: FHIR consent category; DPV consent type.

data_elements.name: regulatory_basis_codes
data_elements.description: FHIR regulatoryBasis or DPV legal-basis IRI, e.g. GDPR Art 6(1)(a).

artifacts.name: Classification block
artifacts.description: Typed flags that tell evaluators which rule family and default decision to apply.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Carried inline on the instrument header and addressed through access_contract_id; no separate identifier.

layers.name: Parties and roles
layers.description: Identify who grants, who may read, who is the data subject, who manages the instrument, who enforces it, and whether parties are individuals, organisations or collections.

findings.name: Party functional roles
findings.description: ODRL requires Agreement to name assigner and assignee; Offer requires assigner. FHIR names grantor (who grants rights), grantee (who must comply with the directive, including obligations), manager (lifecycle), controller (enforcer), and subject (who the consent is about). UMA distinguishes resource owner, requesting party, client, resource server and authorization server, and allows the requesting party to differ from the owner. Party collections may be refined (for example friends over age 18). FHIR comments that grantor/grantee are search conveniences and that fully computable consents list both as actors inside provisions. The Kantara Consent Receipt historically treats the PII principal as issuing a receipt to the controller, whereas ISO 27560 treats the organisation as issuing a receipt to the individual.

questions.text: Who is the grantor, and which ownership, parental-responsibility or delegation record authorises them to grant?
Which party or party collection is the grantee, and are members refined by attributes such as role or age?
Is the data subject a different person from the grantor, as with a parent granting over a child's record?
Which actor manages the instrument through its lifecycle and which actor evaluates reads against it?

data_elements.name: grantor_party_id
data_elements.description: ODRL assigner / FHIR grantor. Must resolve to an ownership or capacity record.

data_elements.name: grantee_party_id
data_elements.description: ODRL assignee / FHIR grantee / UMA requesting party or client.

data_elements.name: subject_party_id
data_elements.description: PII principal or FHIR subject when different from grantor.

data_elements.name: manager_party_id
data_elements.description: FHIR manager; UMA authorization server operator is not automatically the manager.

data_elements.name: enforcer_party_id
data_elements.description: FHIR controller; data holder that evaluates reads.

data_elements.name: party_collection_refinement
data_elements.description: ODRL PartyCollection.refinement.

data_elements.name: ownership_authority_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to ownership/delegation/guardianship record; not stored as title here.

artifacts.name: Party roster
artifacts.description: Resolved party identifiers, roles, collection membership and authority references for one instrument.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Scoped to access_contract_id; each entry keyed by party IRI plus functional role.

layers.name: Grant terms and purpose
layers.description: State the deontic content: what action is permitted, prohibited or obligatory, for which purpose, on which legal basis, and with which purpose-compatibility notes.

findings.name: Permission, prohibition and duty
findings.description: ODRL Rule subclasses are Permission (action MAY be exercised if constraints are satisfied and duties fulfilled), Prohibition (action MUST NOT be exercised; remedies apply if infringed), and Duty (action MUST be exercised; consequences apply if not). A Permission MAY carry duties as pre-conditions. FHIR provision.action, when present, lists controlled actions; if missing, all actions are meant, but the tested FHIR privacy scope is read. This catalogue's purpose is machine-readable permission to read, so the default Action is read/use, with transfer and onward-disclose modelled as separate permissions or prohibitions. ODRL includedIn and implies relations on Actions create inherited conflicts that evaluators MUST detect.

questions.text: Which action or actions does this grant permit, and is read implied by a broader use action?
Must any duty be fulfilled before the permission may be exercised?
Which actions are prohibited for this grantee, notably onward share, archive, or commercial use?

data_elements.name: rule_id
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of one atomic rule so later rules can reference it.

data_elements.name: rule_kind
data_elements.description: permission | prohibition | duty | fhir-provision.

data_elements.name: action_code
data_elements.description: odrl:read, odrl:use, odrl:distribute, fhir consent-action, or Dimension read.

data_elements.name: action_included_in
data_elements.description: ODRL includedIn ancestor, typically use or transfer.

data_elements.name: duty_refs
data_elements.description: Pre-condition duties attached to a permission.

data_elements.name: remedy_refs
data_elements.description: Duties if a prohibition is infringed.

artifacts.name: Deontic rule set
artifacts.description: Atomic permission, prohibition and duty rules with action identifiers and links to duties and remedies.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each rule keyed by rule_id within access_contract_id so duties and remedies can reference it.

findings.name: Purpose limitation and legal basis
findings.description: Purpose is mandatory in ISO 27560 records and in GDPR Articles 5, 6(1)(a), 13 and 14. FHIR provision.purpose uses HL7 PurposeOfUse and requires that a request purpose SHALL NOT conflict with a purpose tag on the data. Recital 32 requires consent for each purpose when processing has multiple purposes; Recital 43 presumes consent is not freely given if operations that should be separable are bundled. Recital 33 allows consent to areas of scientific research when ethical standards apply. Recital 50 addresses further processing compatibility, which is not a substitute for a new consent when the original basis was consent. DPV types Consent as one LegalBasis among others; an access contract that is actually a contract-performance or legal-obligation disclosure MUST not be labelled as consent.

questions.text: For which specific purpose may the grantee read, and is that purpose a primary service purpose or a secondary purpose such as marketing or research?
Is the legal basis consent, explicit consent for special-category data, contract performance, or a non-personal licence?
May the grantee further process for a compatible purpose without a new grant, and if not, what amendment process is required?

data_elements.name: purpose_id
data_elements.description: Stable purpose clause identifier.

data_elements.name: purpose_text
data_elements.description: Human-readable purpose as presented in the notice.

data_elements.name: purpose_category
data_elements.description: DPV Purpose, ISO 27560 purpose type, FHIR PurposeOfUse, or Kantara purposeCategory.

data_elements.name: primary_purpose
data_elements.description: Kantara CR primaryPurpose flag.

data_elements.name: legal_basis
data_elements.description: dpv:Consent, eu-gdpr:A6-1-a, contract, or not-applicable-for-non-personal-asset.

data_elements.name: consent_type
data_elements.description: DPV ExpressedConsent, ExplicitlyExpressedConsent, InformedConsent; Kantara EXPLICIT.

data_elements.name: purpose_compatibility_note
data_elements.description: Whether further processing is claimed compatible; must not silently extend consent.

artifacts.name: Purpose clause
artifacts.description: One purpose with category, legal basis, consent type and compatibility notes; multiple purposes are separate clauses.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by purpose_id within the instrument; one clause per unbundled purpose.

layers.name: Scope selection
layers.description: Partition the grant into concrete slices of objects, classes, labels and time-bounded data, each optionally shaped by a sibling projection policy.

findings.name: Target objects and data meaning
findings.description: ODRL Permission and Prohibition MUST have a target Asset, which may be an AssetCollection with refinement. FHIR provision.data.meaning interprets a reference as instance, related, dependents or authoredby; if data is missing, all data is meant. provision.dataPeriod bounds the clinical or operational time of the data, which is different from Consent.period (when the agreement holds). ISO 27560 requires PII types and storage/retention facts for privacy grants. Scope clauses in this mixin point at registry objects from the ownership model and MUST reference a disclosure-scope/projection policy when a shape other than native is to leave the holder. Frequency or count limits belong with constraints, not with identity of the object.

questions.text: Which registry objects, collections or classes does this clause cover, and how is a reference interpreted (this instance, related, dependents, authored-by)?
Does the clause limit the timeframe of the data (for example only encounters after 2024) separately from the grant's validity window?
Must the permitted read leave the holder only in a named projection or redaction shape?

data_elements.name: scope_clause_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of one slice of the grant.

data_elements.name: target_object_refs
data_elements.description: Registry entry, FHIR resource, ODRL asset or collection source.

data_elements.name: data_meaning
data_elements.description: instance | related | dependents | authoredby | collection-members.

data_elements.name: resource_or_document_class
data_elements.description: FHIR resourceType, documentType, code.

data_elements.name: security_labels
data_elements.description: High-water confidentiality or other privacy tags.

data_elements.name: data_period_start
data_elements.description: Start of data timeframe controlled, distinct from grant validity.

data_elements.name: data_period_end
data_elements.description: End of data timeframe controlled.

data_elements.name: projection_policy_ref
data_elements.description: Sibling disclosure-scope policy; required when output shape is constrained.

data_elements.name: pii_categories
data_elements.description: ISO 27560 / Kantara PII categories for privacy grants.

artifacts.name: Scope clause
artifacts.description: One covered slice: object references, class/label filters, data-period, data-meaning and projection-policy pointer.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by scope_clause_id within the instrument; target_object_refs resolve into the ownership registry.

layers.name: Constraints and obligations
layers.description: Qualify when and where a rule holds, how often it may be exercised, which geographic and retention limits apply, and which duties survive the grant.

findings.name: Temporal, spatial and count constraints
findings.description: ODRL Constraints compare a leftOperand and rightOperand with an operator; Logical Constraints combine them with and, or, xone or andSequence. Typical access-contract operands are dateTime, elapsedTime, count, spatial, and industry-profile operands such as purpose or role. ISO 27560 requires validity duration, jurisdiction, storage locations, processing locations, geographic restrictions and retention period on privacy records. All time values in this mixin use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. Event time (when the constraint applies in the world) is stored separately from observation/ingestion time (when the record was written).

questions.text: From when until when is this rule exercisable, in RFC 3339 with offset, and is that window different from the data-period?
In which jurisdictions or locations may the grantee store or process the read results, and which geographic restrictions apply?
Is there a maximum number of reads or a frequency cap, and how is current status counted?

data_elements.name: constraint_id
data_elements.description: Stable constraint identifier, required if referenced by a logical operand.

data_elements.name: left_operand
data_elements.description: ODRL leftOperand such as dateTime, count, spatial.

data_elements.name: operator
data_elements.description: lt, lteq, eq, gt, gteq, isAnyOf, etc.

data_elements.name: right_operand
data_elements.description: Comparison value; use rightOperandReference when the value must be dereferenced.

data_elements.name: validity_start
data_elements.description: Grant or rule start, inclusive, with offset or Z.

data_elements.name: validity_end
data_elements.description: Grant or rule end; open-ended must be explicit, not a missing date used as an id.

data_elements.name: jurisdiction_codes
data_elements.description: ISO 27560 jurisdiction; processing/storage location codes.

data_elements.name: max_count_or_frequency
data_elements.description: Read-count or rate limit with unit.

artifacts.name: Constraint set
artifacts.description: Atomic and logical constraints including validity window, geography and exercise limits.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each constraint keyed by constraint_id so logical constraints can reference it from within the rule.

findings.name: Duties, retention and onward sharing
findings.description: ISO 27560 requires retention period, recipient third parties and a withdrawal method on privacy records. Kantara receipts record thirdPartyDisclosure and termination text per purpose. ODRL Duty is fulfilled when its action is exercised and constraints are satisfied; unfulfilled duties on a Permission block the Permission; consequences attach if the duty itself is not fulfilled. Typical access-contract duties are: no onward disclosure except named parties, erase or return copies at end of grant, keep the read confidential, and notify the grantor of a breach. Duties may outlive the permission (end-of-grant erasure). This mixin records the duty and its evidence of discharge; escalation of a breach is the enforcement sibling.

questions.text: May the grantee disclose the read results to any third party, and if so to whom and for which purpose?
What must the grantee do when the grant ends or is withdrawn, and by which deadline?
Has this duty been fulfilled, on what evidence, at what event time?

data_elements.name: obligation_id
data_elements.description: Duty clause identifier.

data_elements.name: duty_action
data_elements.description: erase, notify, compensate, attribute, nextPolicy, or Dimension-coded duty.

data_elements.name: duty_kind
data_elements.description: precondition | ongoing | post-termination | remedy | consequence.

data_elements.name: onward_sharing_allowed
data_elements.description: False unless named recipients are listed.

data_elements.name: named_recipients
data_elements.description: ISO 27560 recipient third parties.

data_elements.name: retention_period
data_elements.description: ISO 27560 retention; may survive withdrawal when another legal basis applies.

data_elements.name: consequence_ref
data_elements.description: Follow-on duty if this duty is not fulfilled.

data_elements.name: discharge_evidence_ref
data_elements.description: Artefact proving erasure or notification.

artifacts.name: Obligation clause
artifacts.description: One grantee duty with kind, deadline, recipients, retention and discharge evidence pointer.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by obligation_id within the instrument; discharge evidence is referenced, not embedded.

bundles.name: Consent evidence
bundles.description: Capture the human or authorised act behind a privacy-flavour instrument: how assent was indicated, by whom, with what notice, and how a portable receipt is issued. Not required for non-personal usage licences classified as such.
bundles.rationale: GDPR Article 7(1) demonstration, ISO/IEC TS 27560 event records and ISO/IEC 29184 notice controls require the human act behind a privacy-flavour grant to be recorded and evidenced separately from the grant terms.

layers.name: Expression and indication
layers.description: Record how and when consent or refusal was indicated, including method, channel, language and evidence artefact.

findings.name: Consent indication event
findings.description: GDPR Recital 32 requires a clear affirmative act; silence, pre-ticked boxes and inactivity are not consent. DPV records hasIndicationMethod, isIndicationTime and isIndicatedBy, plus ConsentStatus. ISO 27560 event section requires event time, event type, event state, entity and validity duration. Kantara CR records consentTimestamp, collectionMethod and consentType. Indication (event) time MUST be stored separately from record-creation (observation/ingestion) time. Both use RFC 3339 with seconds and offset or Z. A consent record that lacks an indication event cannot demonstrate Article 7(1) compliance.

questions.text: By what affirmative act, on which channel, and in which language was consent given, refused or withdrawn?
What is the RFC 3339 event time of the indication, and what is the distinct ingestion time of this record?
What artefact proves the act, and is it a hash of a UI snapshot, a cryptographic signature, or a verbal-consent attestation?

data_elements.name: indication_event_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the expression event.

data_elements.name: indication_method
data_elements.description: Unticked checkbox click, wet signature, oral, API POST, GPC signal, etc.

data_elements.name: indication_channel
data_elements.description: Kantara collectionMethod / ISO collection_method.

data_elements.name: indication_time
data_elements.description: Event time of the act.

data_elements.name: ingested_time
data_elements.description: Observation/ingestion time of this record.

data_elements.name: indicated_by_party_id
data_elements.description: Actor who performed the act.

data_elements.name: indication_result
data_elements.description: given | refused | withdrawn | reaffirmed.

data_elements.name: language_tag
data_elements.description: ISO 27560 language of the notice and act.

data_elements.name: evidence_artefact_ref
data_elements.description: Log, signed payload, recording reference, or UI snapshot hash.

artifacts.name: Indication evidence pack
artifacts.description: Method, channel, times, actor, result and a pointer to the stored proof of the affirmative act.
artifacts.identity_strategy: One pack per indication_event_id, bound to access_contract_id and stamped with distinct indication and ingestion times.

layers.name: Capacity and authorised actors
layers.description: Record who was legally able to express the grant, including children, guardians and delegates, without duplicating the ownership sibling's authority registry.

findings.name: Acting capacity
findings.description: GDPR Article 8 sets a 16-year default for information-society services, which Member States may lower to 13; Recital 38 requires specific protection of children and notes that parental consent is not needed for preventive or counselling services offered directly to a child. FHIR allows RelatedPerson, Practitioner and Organization grantors and a verification block recording who verified the decision with whom. ISO 29184 and 27560 expect the PII principal or an authorised representative. This mixin records capacity_code (self, parental-holder, guardian, delegate, organisational-officer) and a reference to the ownership/delegation record. It does not decide whether that record is valid.

questions.text: Did the acting party consent as self, as holder of parental responsibility, as guardian, or as a recorded delegate?
If the principal is a child, which Article 8 age threshold applies, and is this a counselling service that does not require parental consent?
Was the grantor decision verified, by whom, with whom, and at what time?

data_elements.name: capacity_code
data_elements.description: self | parental-holder | guardian | delegate | organisational-officer.

data_elements.name: principal_age_band
data_elements.description: child-under-13 | 13-to-15 | 16-plus | adult | unknown. Do not use a date of birth as the contract id.

data_elements.name: applicable_age_of_consent
data_elements.description: Member State Article 8 value 13-16 when the grant is an ISS service.

data_elements.name: acting_party_id
data_elements.description: Person who clicked, signed or spoke.

data_elements.name: authority_record_ref
data_elements.description: Required unless capacity_code is self.

data_elements.name: verification_status
data_elements.description: FHIR verification.verified.

data_elements.name: verified_with_party_id
data_elements.description: FHIR verifiedWith.

data_elements.name: verification_time
data_elements.description: When capacity or grantor decision was checked.

artifacts.name: Capacity assertion
artifacts.description: Claimed capacity, age-band, authority-record pointer and optional verification of the acting party.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound to access_contract_id and acting_party_id; authority itself is addressed by authority_record_ref in the ownership sibling.

layers.name: Informedness and consent qualities
layers.description: Record the notice that made the choice informed and the qualitative tests that determine whether the indication is legally usable as consent.

findings.name: Notice reference and validity qualities
findings.description: Informed consent requires that the principal knows at least the controller's identity and the purposes (Recital 42) and, under Articles 13 and 14, recipients, transfers, storage period, rights including withdrawal, and automated decision-making. ISO 29184 specifies notice content, timing, language, accessibility and that consent must be fair, demonstrable, transparent, unambiguous and revocable. ISO 27560 requires a privacy_notice reference on the record. Recital 43: consent is not freely given in a clear imbalance (especially public authorities) or where a contract is conditioned on unnecessary processing, or where separable operations are bundled. Article 7(2) requires a consent request in a written declaration to be clearly distinguishable. Article 7(3) requires that withdrawal be as easy as giving consent and that the principal is informed of the withdrawal right beforehand. These qualities are assessments, not automatic consequences of storing a record. A GPC or similar preference signal (ISO 27560 Annex F) may be a control input; treating it as GDPR consent is an unproven alignment and MUST be flagged.

questions.text: Which privacy notice version was in force at indication time, and did it identify the controller, purposes, recipients, retention, transfers and withdrawal right?
Was consent separate from contract terms, unbundled by purpose, and free of a clear power imbalance?
Is there a withdrawal path that is as easy as the give-path, and was the principal told about it before indicating?

data_elements.name: privacy_notice_ref
data_elements.description: Notice in force at indication time; ISO 27560 mandatory for privacy records.

data_elements.name: notice_version
data_elements.description: Version or hash of the notice actually shown.

data_elements.name: controller_identity_presented
data_elements.description: Whether identity of controller was shown.

data_elements.name: withdrawal_method_presented
data_elements.description: Article 7(3) prior information.

data_elements.name: freely_given_assessment
data_elements.description: pass | fail | not-assessed, with imbalance and bundling flags.

data_elements.name: specific_unbundled
data_elements.description: Separate indication per purpose when required.

data_elements.name: unambiguous_affirmative
data_elements.description: Not silence or pre-ticked.

data_elements.name: as_easy_to_withdraw
data_elements.description: Withdrawal path complexity relative to give-path.

data_elements.name: special_category_explicit
data_elements.description: Article 9(2)(a) extra bar.

data_elements.name: preference_signal_codes
data_elements.description: GPC or similar; do not auto-promote to consent.

artifacts.name: Notice binding and quality assessment
artifacts.description: Pinned notice version plus structured assessments of freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, distinguishable and withdrawable.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Binds privacy_notice_ref plus notice_version to the indication_event_id it made informed.

layers.name: Record, receipt and demonstration
layers.description: Separate the controller's integrity-controlled consent record from the portable receipt issued to the principal, and support Article 7(1) demonstration.

findings.name: Consent record versus consent receipt
findings.description: ISO 27560 defines a consent record as the organisation's integrity-controlled documentation (header, processing, parties, events) and a consent receipt as an authoritative document used to communicate existence or content of a record. A 27560-conformant receipt only mandatorily needs receipt identifier and schema version; profiles such as DPV-27560 make record fields mandatory on receipts so the principal receives a usable copy. Kantara CR 1.1 defined a JSON receipt issued in the opposite narrative direction (principal to controller). DPVCG documents that either party may keep records or issue receipts, and that ISO 27560 does not specify an exchange protocol. Demonstration under Article 7(1) and Recital 42 is a duty of the controller and is not satisfied by a receipt the principal lost.

questions.text: Where is the integrity-controlled consent record kept, and what proof binds it to the indication event?
Was a portable receipt issued, with which schema, to whom, at what time, on which channel?
Which fields of the record are copied into the receipt, and which are omitted for confidentiality?

data_elements.name: consent_record_id
data_elements.description: ISO 27560 record id; may equal access_contract_id for privacy flavour.

data_elements.name: consent_receipt_id
data_elements.description: Distinct from the record id.

data_elements.name: receipt_schema
data_elements.description: KI-CR-v1.1.0 or dpv-27560:receipt-eu-gdpr.

data_elements.name: receipt_issued_to
data_elements.description: Usually the PII principal.

data_elements.name: receipt_issued_time
data_elements.description: Event time of issuance.

data_elements.name: record_integrity_proof
data_elements.description: Hash, signature or WORM store reference for demonstration.

data_elements.name: delivery_channel
data_elements.description: email, wallet, portal download, paper.

artifacts.name: Consent receipt
artifacts.description: Authoritative copy delivered to the principal; must not be mistaken for the integrity master record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by consent_receipt_id in an identifier space distinct from consent_record_id and access_contract_id.

bundles.name: Lifecycle
bundles.description: Describe how a grant is proposed, activated, amended, withdrawn, expired, superseded or invalidated, including rare succession cases.
bundles.rationale: FHIR Consent.status, DPV ConsentStatus and ISO/IEC TS 27560 events all encode state transitions, so activation, amendment and termination are grouped as their own concern rather than as flags on the terms.

layers.name: States and activation
layers.description: Enumerate status vocabularies and the transition from notice and offer to a live grant.

findings.name: Status and activation path
findings.description: FHIR Consent.status is required: draft, active, inactive, not-done, entered-in-error, unknown. DPV ConsentStatus includes requested, given, withdrawn and related states; the DPV-27560 lifecycle chart starts at notice, then given or refused, then reaffirmation or termination. ODRL Offer does not grant; Agreement does. UMA request_submitted means the owner has not yet set or extended policy conditions. A contract is exercisable only when status is an active/given equivalent, validity constraints are satisfied, required duties are fulfilled, and (for privacy flavour) consent has not been withdrawn. entered-in-error and unknown MUST be treated as not authorising reads.

questions.text: Is the instrument in an exercisable status at the evaluation instant, and which vocabulary is being used?
Was activation by grantor signature, by assignee acceptance of an Offer, by UMA owner policy-setting, or by a verbal consent later recorded?
When was consent last reaffirmed or re-verified, and is reaffirmation required on notice change?

data_elements.name: status_code
data_elements.description: draft | offered | requested | active | refused | inactive | withdrawn | expired | superseded | entered-in-error | unknown.

data_elements.name: status_vocabulary
data_elements.description: fhir-consent-state | dpv-consent-status | dimension-map.

data_elements.name: activation_time
data_elements.description: Event time the grant became exercisable.

data_elements.name: fhir_date
data_elements.description: FHIR fully executed date; complement, do not replace, RFC 3339 activation_time.

data_elements.name: reaffirmation_time
data_elements.description: Last confirmation event.

data_elements.name: status_reason
data_elements.description: Why the current state holds.

artifacts.name: Lifecycle status record
artifacts.description: Current status, vocabulary mapping, activation and reaffirmation times.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Single current-state record per access_contract_id; historical transitions live in the event log.

layers.name: Amendment and termination
layers.description: Model scope changes, withdrawal, expiry, supersession, invalidation, and unresolved succession cases.

findings.name: Withdrawal, expiry, supersession and succession
findings.description: Article 7(3): the principal may withdraw at any time; withdrawal is as easy as giving; withdrawal does not make prior processing unlawful. Article 17 and Recital 65: after withdrawal, erasure applies unless another basis holds. ISO 27560 treats expiry, withdrawal, controller termination and authority invalidation as event types that end validity. FHIR uses inactive, not-done and entered-in-error rather than a dedicated withdrawn code. Supersession MUST point at the replacing instrument. Rare cases without a single primary encoding, and therefore gaps unless a profile supplies them: death of a natural-person grantor (GDPR Recital 27 leaves deceased persons to Member State law); corporate merger of an organisational grantor or grantee; joint-controller arrangements; restoration after accidental withdrawal; and research broad-consent remaining valid for an area after a protocol amendment (Recital 33). UMA Section 3.7 allows RFC 7009 revocation of RPT, refresh token or PCT, which is an exercise-layer cutoff, not a substitute for the consent-record event.

questions.text: If the grant is not live, what kind of termination occurred, at what effective time, issued by whom?
Does this termination require erasure or return of copies, or does another legal basis keep the data?
If this instrument was superseded or amended, which instrument is now authoritative, and was the change agreed or unilateral?
If the grantor has died, lost capacity, or the organisation has merged, is there a jurisdictional rule that continues, freezes or voids the grant?

data_elements.name: termination_event_id
data_elements.description: Event that ended the grant.

data_elements.name: termination_kind
data_elements.description: withdrawn | expired | superseded | invalidated | refused | entered-in-error | owner-revoked | death-or-succession.

data_elements.name: termination_time
data_elements.description: Effective event time; prior reads remain lawful if they were in-scope then.

data_elements.name: termination_issuer
data_elements.description: Grantor, principal, controller, authority or system-expiry.

data_elements.name: termination_reason
data_elements.description: Reason as given by issuer.

data_elements.name: replacing_contract_id
data_elements.description: Required when kind is superseded.

data_elements.name: prior_processing_lawful
data_elements.description: Article 7(3) default true for withdrawal.

data_elements.name: propagation_status
data_elements.description: pending | confirmed | partial | failed for holder cutoff.

artifacts.name: Revocation or termination notice
artifacts.description: Issuer, kind, effective time, reason, replacement pointer and propagation status.
artifacts.identity_strategy: One notice per termination_event_id referencing access_contract_id and, when superseded, replacing_contract_id.

bundles.name: Exercise and propagation
bundles.description: The operating surface: decide whether a concrete read is covered, issue or revoke entitlement tokens, and propagate cutoff to every holder of copies.
bundles.rationale: ODRL evaluation, FHIR provision matching and UMA token issuance are where an instrument becomes a decision, so verification, tokens and cutoff propagation are grouped as the operating surface.

layers.name: Grant verification
layers.description: Evaluate a proposed read against live rules without leaking unnecessary contract content.

findings.name: Read coverage decision
findings.description: An ODRL Evaluator determines whether rules meet their intended action performance: a Permission is exercisable if refinements and constraints are satisfied and duties fulfilled; a Prohibition is infringed if its action is exercised while constraints are satisfied. FHIR evaluation uses base decision plus nested exception provisions, matching actor, action, purpose, data, labels and periods. UMA authorization assessment intersects registered client scopes, ticket scopes and requested scopes, then applies owner policy conditions that this mixin supplies. FHIR notes that enforcement may use OAuth, UMA or XACML and is out of Consent resource scope. Default-deny must still fail closed on unknown status, missing authority, unfulfilled duty, purpose mismatch, or expired window. A verification response SHOULD return only validity, a scope fingerprint, and any obligation identifiers the caller must still obey, not the full consent evidence.

questions.text: At evaluation instant T, does a live instrument permit this requester to perform this action on these objects for this purpose?
If denied, which fail-closed reason applied, and is the caller allowed to see that reason?
Which obligation identifiers remain binding even after a permit, such as no-onward-share or local-cache TTL?

data_elements.name: evaluation_request_id
data_elements.description: Id of this verification call.

data_elements.name: requested_action
data_elements.description: Usually read.

data_elements.name: requested_object_refs
data_elements.description: Objects the caller wants to read.

data_elements.name: requested_purpose
data_elements.description: Purpose of this access attempt.

data_elements.name: evaluation_instant
data_elements.description: Time T used for constraint evaluation.

data_elements.name: decision
data_elements.description: permit | deny | need-info | not-applicable.

data_elements.name: matched_rule_ids
data_elements.description: Rules that justified the decision.

data_elements.name: scope_fingerprint
data_elements.description: Non-invertible digest of matched scope for audit.

data_elements.name: deny_reason_codes
data_elements.description: expired | withdrawn | purpose-mismatch | duty-unfulfilled | out-of-scope | no-authority.

artifacts.name: Validity token or decision record
artifacts.description: Minimal permit/deny result with scope fingerprint; omits parties' sensitive evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: One record per evaluation_request_id; carries scope_fingerprint instead of the instrument identifiers it evaluated.

layers.name: Tokens and revocation propagation
layers.description: Project the instrument into exercisable tokens and ensure every downstream holder cuts off after revocation or expiry.

findings.name: Entitlement tokens and cutoff
findings.description: UMA issues an RPT unique to requesting party, client, authorization server, resource server and resource owner; permissions on the token are opaque to the client. Refresh MUST NOT re-run authorization assessment. RFC 7009 revocation, with UMA token type hint pct, cuts tokens. FHIR expects signatures and ceremony stages in Provenance, DocumentReference or Contract attachments rather than in Consent itself. After withdrawal or expiry, every holder of data under the grant must be notified and must confirm cutoff; ISO 27560 does not define that protocol, so this mixin records propagation status as an operating concern and leaves transport to implementations. Partial propagation is a first-class state, not a success. Cached validity tokens MUST expire no later than the grant window and SHOULD be revoked when the instrument is withdrawn.

questions.text: Is there a current entitlement token, of which kind, expiring when, and is it unique to this requesting party and client?
Which parties currently hold copies or caches under this grant, and which have confirmed cutoff?
Were RPTs, refresh tokens and persisted-claims tokens revoked, at what time, and did refresh continue to mint access without re-assessment?

data_elements.name: entitlement_token_id
data_elements.description: RPT or Dimension validity token; not the contract id.

data_elements.name: token_kind
data_elements.description: uma-rpt | refresh | pct | validity-token.

data_elements.name: token_expires_at
data_elements.description: Must not exceed grant validity_end.

data_elements.name: holder_party_ids
data_elements.description: Every known holder that must receive cutoff.

data_elements.name: propagation_status
data_elements.description: not-required | pending | confirmed | partial | failed.

data_elements.name: cutoff_confirmed_time
data_elements.description: When a holder acknowledged no further reads.

data_elements.name: token_revoked_time
data_elements.description: RFC 7009 or local revoke event time.

artifacts.name: Revocation propagation ledger
artifacts.description: Per-holder cutoff acknowledgements and token revocation times for one termination event.
artifacts.identity_strategy: One ledger per termination_event_id, with entries keyed by holder party IRI and acknowledgement time.

bundles.name: Provenance, quality and interoperability
bundles.description: Keep an event history, distinguish a stored record from a valid consent, and document alignments and conflicts with external standards.
bundles.rationale: A complete record can still be legally invalid and alignment is not conformance, so event history, quality flags and external mappings are kept as a distinct bundle rather than folded into the instrument.

layers.name: Provenance and quality
layers.description: Trace who recorded what, and flag when a record cannot be treated as valid consent.

findings.name: Event history and validity quality
findings.description: ISO 27560 and DPV require an event list (notice, given, withdrawn, reaffirmed, expired, invalidated). FHIR recommends Provenance to track changes to Consent and allows sourceAttachment or sourceReference chains back to a paper form, CDA, Contract or prior Consent; applications MUST NOT assume they are authorised to walk the chain. A complete record can still be legally invalid (bundled, imbalanced, child without capacity, notice mismatch). Quality flags therefore separate: record_complete, demonstration_possible, legal_validity_assessed, and assessment_result. Agents MUST NOT treat record_complete as permit.

questions.text: Which events have occurred on this instrument, in order, with event time versus recorded time?
Are all mandatory fields for the chosen profile present so demonstration is possible?
Has legal validity been assessed, with what result, and if uncertain what is missing (capacity, unbundling, notice, affirmative act)?

data_elements.name: event_id
data_elements.description: One lifecycle event.

data_elements.name: event_type
data_elements.description: notice-shown | requested | given | refused | amended | withdrawn | expired | verified | duty-discharged.

data_elements.name: event_time
data_elements.description: World time of the event.

data_elements.name: recorded_time
data_elements.description: Ingestion time.

data_elements.name: actor_id
data_elements.description: Who performed or recorded the event.

data_elements.name: source_artefact_ref
data_elements.description: Paper scan, CDA, prior consent, signed Offer.

data_elements.name: record_complete
data_elements.description: Mandatory 27560/GDPR fields present.

data_elements.name: legal_validity_assessed
data_elements.description: Whether qualities were evaluated.

data_elements.name: legal_validity_result
data_elements.description: valid | invalid | uncertain | not-applicable-licence.

artifacts.name: Consent and grant event log
artifacts.description: Append-only events with dual timestamps, actors and source artefact pointers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Append-only series keyed by event_id within access_contract_id, ordered by event_time with recorded_time retained separately.

layers.name: Alignments and conflicts
layers.description: Record how external standards map onto this mixin and where they disagree, without claiming conformance.

findings.name: Mapping conflicts and non-conformance
findings.description: Alignments, not conformance claims: ODRL Agreement maps to the instrument and deontic rules; ISO 27560 and DPV-27560 map to privacy-flavour records and receipts; FHIR Consent maps to healthcare privacy directives and nested provisions; Kantara CR 1.1 maps to receipt JSON; UMA 2.0 maps to exercise. Documented conflicts: (1) Kantara CR narrative is principal-to-controller, ISO 27560 is organisation-to-principal. (2) ODRL Party may be a legal person; GDPR consent cannot. (3) FHIR grantee is the party who must comply, ODRL assignee is the recipient of permission; they overlap but are not identical. (4) FHIR status has no withdrawn code. (5) ODRL conflict perm can override a Prohibition, which may violate a privacy default-deny. (6) ISO 27560 lawful_basis is optional even though a consent record implies consent. (7) UMA refresh does not re-evaluate policy. (8) Kantara CR 1.1 terminology is known not to match GDPR field-for-field. Implementations MAY project to these models; they MUST record the profile URI and MUST NOT assert ISO, GDPR, FHIR or ODRL conformance without a separate evidence artefact.

questions.text: Which external standards is this instance projecting to, in which mode, under which profile URI?
Which documented conflicts affect this instance, for example legal-person grantor on a privacy-consent flavour?
Is any conformance to ISO 27560, GDPR, FHIR or ODRL actually evidenced, and by which artefact?

data_elements.name: alignment_target
data_elements.description: odrl-2.2 | iso-27560 | iso-29184 | fhir-consent-r5 | dpv-consent | kantara-cr-1.1 | uma-2.0.

data_elements.name: alignment_mode
data_elements.description: align | extend | reference | exclude.

data_elements.name: conflict_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of a recorded conflict.

data_elements.name: conflict_description
data_elements.description: How the external term differs.

data_elements.name: conformance_claim
data_elements.description: none | claimed | evidenced. Default none.

data_elements.name: conformance_evidence_ref
data_elements.description: Required if claim is evidenced.

artifacts.name: Alignment and conflict register
artifacts.description: Per-standard mapping mode, known conflicts and any evidenced conformance claim. Pure reference data when no projection is generated.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Entries keyed by alignment_target within the instrument profile; conflicts keyed by conflict_id.

functions.name: Grant verification
functions.description: Decide whether a specific requested read is covered by a live access contract and return a minimal validity result.
preconditions: Requester identity is authenticated by a sibling identity system.
Target objects are registered in the ownership model.
Evaluation instant is an RFC 3339 timestamp.
effects: Does not modify the instrument.
Emits an evaluation event to the audit sibling.
MUST fail closed on unknown, expired, withdrawn, duty-unfulfilled, purpose mismatch, or missing authority.

functions.name: Consent capture
functions.description: Record an indication event with evidence, capacity, notice binding and dual timestamps, producing or updating a consent record.
preconditions: For privacy flavour, indication is an affirmative act.
If capacity is not self, ownership sibling returns a live authority record.
effects: Creates or appends an event to the consent record.
Does not by itself authorise reads until activation rules are met.
Sets legal_validity_assessed only if quality tests are run.

functions.name: Consent receipt delivery
functions.description: Issue a portable, profiled copy of the consent record to the principal or grantor.
preconditions: Master record exists and is integrity-protected.
Recipient is the PII principal, grantor, or a recorded delegate.
effects: Creates a receipt identifier distinct from the record identifier.
Does not change grant status.
Logs issuance for demonstration.

functions.name: Contract activation
functions.description: Transition an Offer, draft or requested instrument into an exercisable Agreement after required parties and evidence are present.
preconditions: Instrument is an Offer, draft or requested state.
Privacy flavour has a captured given-indication unless classified as a non-consent licence.
effects: Sets status to active/given.
Starts validity window.
Makes grant-verification eligible to return permit.

functions.name: Scope amendment
functions.description: Replace covered objects, purposes, constraints or projection references by agreement, retiring or superseding the previous instrument version.
preconditions: Amendment mode is agreed-by-parties or grantor-unilateral as allowed by the original terms.
Privacy-flavour purpose expansion requires a new indication.
effects: Writes a new version or successor id.
Marks the prior version superseded.
Does not rewrite historical evaluation events.

functions.name: Revocation propagation
functions.description: End a grant from an effective time forward, revoke entitlement tokens, and collect cutoff confirmation from every known holder.
preconditions: Issuer is the grantor, the PII principal, a recorded delegate, a supervisory invalidation, or the system clock for expiry.
effects: Status becomes withdrawn, expired, superseded or invalidated.
Prior in-scope processing remains lawful when kind is withdrawn.
Triggers post-termination duties such as erasure.
Revokes RPTs, refresh tokens and validity tokens.
Leaves transport of holder notification to the implementation; records ack state here.

functions.name: Obligation discharge
functions.description: Record that a grantee duty, especially end-of-grant erasure, has been fulfilled and evidenced.
preconditions: Evidence artefact is retrievable by the audit sibling.
effects: Marks the duty fulfilled or failed.
May unblock a Permission if the duty was a pre-condition.
May close an enforcement case in the sibling model when referenced.

functions.name: Conflict evaluation
functions.description: Detect Permission/Prohibition/Action-inheritance clashes and apply the instrument's conflict strategy or fail invalid.
preconditions: Rules and action includedIn/implies graph are available.
effects: Does not change stored rules.
Returns invalid when strategy is invalid or when privacy default-deny forbids perm-overrides-prohibition without an explicit profile.

composition.purpose: Grantor authority, parental responsibility, guardianship and delegation resolve against the ownership sibling. This mixin stores only capacity_code and an authority_record_ref. A grant from a party who is not the holder or an authorised actor is void.
Scope clauses do not encode redaction or projection shapes. When a non-native disclosure shape is required, projection_policy_ref points at the disclosure-scope sibling.

Every capture, activation, amendment, verification, receipt issuance, revocation and duty-discharge event is logged in the audit sibling. This mixin stores the event identifiers needed for demonstration, not the full audit warehouse.
Out-of-scope reads, infringed prohibitions and undischarged post-termination duties escalate as cases in the enforcement sibling. This mixin only records duty state and deny reasons.
The general contract primitive supplies offer/acceptance mechanics; this mixin specialises it for read permission, consent evidence and revocation propagation.

Map Policy/Agreement, assigner/assignee, Permission/Prohibition/Duty, target, constraint and conflict. Do not treat ODRL legal-person Parties as GDPR consent. Do not claim ODRL profile conformance without a profile IRI.
Map privacy-flavour records and receipts, events, purposes, parties, retention, jurisdiction and withdrawal method. ISO 27560 specifies no exchange protocol.
Privacy notices and the process of asking for consent are governed by 29184. This mixin stores privacy_notice_ref and notice_version only.

Map identifier, status, grantor, grantee, manager, controller, period, decision, nested provisions, purpose, data meaning, verification and policyBasis. Exclude FHIR treatment and research-participation ceremony except when used as a privacy directive.
Map Consent as LegalBasis, ConsentStatus, ConsentRecord, ConsentReceipt, indication relations and the DPV-27560 profiles including the EU GDPR receipt profile.
Map receipt JSON fields for purposes, PII categories, controllers and termination. Record the direction conflict with ISO 27560 and the known GDPR field mismatch.

UMA supplies permission tickets, RPTs, claims gathering and RFC 7009 revocation as an exercise projection. Policy-condition content is this mixin. Refresh-without-reassessment is an operating constraint.

Excluded from this mixin: legitimate interest, legal obligation, vital interest, public task and official authority are not consent and are not this mixin. An access contract may cite them only as legal_basis not-consent so that withdrawal and demonstration rules are not misapplied.
Excluded from this mixin: authentication and identity proofing of grantor, grantee and requesting party are out of scope. Functions assume a resolved party IRI.

owner_package_requirements: The data owner is the grantor and the steward of every contract over their objects.
No registry or operator may create permission beyond what ownership-sibling delegation records allow.
A FHIR-style manager or registry operator may store and version instruments but cannot originate grantor assent.
Reads of contract data follow the same grantor rule.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Every instance declares the profile IRI that interprets its terms (ODRL profile, DPV-27560 profile, FHIR version or Dimension profile IRI); access_contract_id, consent_record_id, consent_receipt_id, entitlement_token_id and indication_event_id occupy distinct identifier spaces and are never interchanged.
registry_links: vr.wm-xct-002 registry entry for the Access Contract / Consent mixin (WM-XCT-002).
Sibling registry entries referenced by composition: world.ownership, world.disclosure-scope, world.access-audit, world.access-enforcement, world.legal-basis, world.identity.

canonicalization_rules: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; event time and observation/ingestion time are stored as separate fields whenever an act is recorded.
Identifiers follow the mastering-system-first priority; a date is never used as an identifier and receipt or token identifiers are never reused as the instrument id.
Each instrument declares schema_profile_uri and instrument_version so that ODRL, FHIR and ISO 27560 projections of the same JSON are read under the intended vocabulary.
patch_rules: Scope, purpose and constraint expansion on a privacy-flavour grant requires a new indication; narrowing by the grantor may be unilateral if the original terms allow.
Amendment writes a new version or successor id and marks the prior version superseded; supersession MUST point at the replacing instrument.
Status transitions to entered-in-error are manager corrections with provenance, not silent deletes, and historical evaluation events are not rewritten.
compatibility_rules: Projection to ODRL, ISO/IEC TS 27560, ISO/IEC 29184, FHIR, DPV, Kantara CR or UMA is alignment, not conformance; the profile URI MUST be recorded and conformance MUST NOT be asserted without a separate evidence artefact.

Documented conflicts (receipt direction, legal-person grantor, grantee versus assignee, missing withdrawn status, perm-over-prohibition, optional lawful_basis, refresh-without-reassessment, Kantara field mismatch) travel with any projection.

identity_priority: Authoritative mastering-system identifier first: ISO 27560 record id, FHIR Consent.identifier, or ODRL Policy.uid IRI.
Then a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension.
A date is not an identifier.
Receipt identifiers and token identifiers are never reused as the instrument id.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. Store event time and observation/ingestion time as separate fields whenever an act is recorded.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: access_contract_id is unique in the mastering system and globally unique when it is an IRI. consent_receipt_id, entitlement_token_id and indication_event_id occupy distinct identifier spaces.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Consent records used for demonstration MUST be integrity-protected (hash, signature or equivalent). Receipts are authoritative copies, not alternative masters. Superseded versions remain immutable for audit.

policies: Fail closed: unknown status, missing authority reference, unfulfilled pre-condition duty, purpose mismatch, expired window, or unverified child-capacity yields deny.
Do not treat a stored record or receipt as legally valid consent until quality flags are assessed. Alignment with ODRL, ISO, FHIR, DPV or Kantara is not conformance.
Withdrawal is as easy as giving consent; withdrawal is not retroactive; post-termination duties still run.
Token and cache lifetimes MUST NOT exceed the grant window and MUST be revoked on withdrawal even if refresh would otherwise mint new access without re-assessment.

read: Grantor and recorded delegates may read the full instrument and evidence.
Grantee may read the entitlement projection (what they may access now) but not other grantors' instruments or consent evidence they do not need.
Enforcers receive validity and scope fingerprint only.
Auditors and supervisory authorities read under a separate legal basis, not under this mixin.
create: Only a grantor, or an actor with a live ownership-sibling authority record, may create a grant.
A would-be grantee may create a draft Offer or request; it does not authorise reads until activation.
Managers may insert integrity envelopes but not fabricate indication events.
update: Scope, purpose and constraint expansion on a privacy-flavour grant requires a new indication.
Narrowing by the grantor may be unilateral if original terms allow.
Status transitions to entered-in-error are manager corrections with provenance, not silent deletes.
delete: Instruments are not physically deleted while demonstration, audit or post-termination duties require them.
After retention of the record itself expires, delete or anonymise per the audit and retention sibling; revocation notices remain as tombstones.
Tokens and cached validity projections are deleted or revoked at cutoff.

roles.name: grantor
responsibilities: Indicate consent or execute the Agreement.

roles.name: grantee
responsibilities: Fulfil duties including no onward sharing and end-of-grant erasure.
Accept Offers when the subtype requires acceptance.

roles.name: capacity-actor
responsibilities: Act for a child or principal under a recorded parental, guardian or delegation authority.

roles.name: manager
responsibilities: Maintain integrity, versioning and receipt issuance.

roles.name: enforcer
responsibilities: Propagate cutoff to holders they control.

roles.name: requesting-party
responsibilities: Present claims when the exercise path is UMA-like.
Use a client that does not reuse another party's PCT or RPT.

roles.name: auditor
responsibilities: Read demonstration packs and event logs.
Must not convert audit access into a data-read grant.

access.default_rule: Contract records and consent evidence are confidential to the grantor. Any other read of those records requires its own access contract. Evaluation APIs return fingerprints, not evidence.
exceptions: Supervisory authority or court order under a non-consent legal basis.
Enforcer need-to-know for a named evaluation request.
Emergency break-glass is not modelled here; if used, it is an enforcement-sibling exception and cannot mint a backdated consent.
audit_requirements: Log every create, activate, amend, verify, receipt, withdraw and duty-discharge with event time, recorded time, actor and outcome.
Retain demonstration packs at least as long as the processing they authorised plus applicable statutory limitation.
Integrity failures on the master record are themselves auditable incidents.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md for Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL.
Read the specification at Specification URL for instrument, consent-evidence and lifecycle semantics.
Use Interface URL only as a projection; do not treat JSON, MCP, MongoDB or Git layout as the model.
Follow Processes URL for capture, verification, receipt and revocation sequences before exercising any read.

coverage.claim: Wide-union context structure for an access-contract and consent mixin, grounded in W3C ODRL 2.2, EU GDPR, HL7 FHIR R5 Consent, ISO/IEC TS 27560:2023, ISO/IEC 29184:2020, W3C DPV-27560, Kantara UMA 2.0 and Kantara Consent Receipt 1.1. Sufficient for an agent to identify, classify, compose, verify, capture, receipt, amend and revoke a read-permission instrument, with documented conflicts and explicit gaps. Not a claim of legal completeness or of conformance to any one standard.

checklist.notes: Master-system id, IRI and Dimension ULID priority; distinct record, receipt, token and event identifier spaces; dates forbidden as identifiers.
Offer/draft/requested/active/withdrawn/expired/superseded/entered-in-error plus DPV notice-given-refused-reaffirm path. Succession after death or merger marked as a gap.
Grantor, grantee, subject, manager, enforcer, requesting party, collections, nested provisions, duty-on-permission, receipt-of-record, supersession.
RFC 3339 event versus ingestion time; grant validity window versus data-period; count/frequency status; token expiry.
Indication evidence, sourceAttachment/sourceReference chain, event log, integrity proof, FHIR verification history.
Stewardship by grantor; authority referenced out to ownership sibling; registry cannot mint permission.
ODRL constraint/duty evaluation, FHIR provision matching, GDPR quality tests, completeness versus legal validity flags, conflict strategy.
Default confidential contract records; evaluation fingerprint; exception list; AGENTS.md bootstrap.
ISO 27560 retention on processing; post-termination erasure duty; instrument tombstones; token deletion at cutoff.
Alignments to ODRL, 27560, 29184, FHIR, DPV, Kantara CR, UMA with an explicit non-conformance default.
Article 8 13-16 range, parental/guardian/delegate capacity, FHIR verification; counselling exception noted.
Unbundled purposes, special-category explicit consent, research-area consent, further-processing warning.

known_omissions: Full ISO 27560 and 29184 clause text is paywalled; field inventory is grounded in ISO catalogue pages plus the DPVCG mapping, not a line-by-line annex transcription.
EDPB Guidelines 05/2020 on consent were not fetched; qualitative tests use GDPR recitals and articles only.
ePrivacy/cookie-specific consent, CPRA 'share' opt-out, and LGPD/APPI/PIPL overlays are not modelled beyond jurisdiction and alignment hooks.
IHE BPPC and HL7 CDA ConsentDirective are mentioned by FHIR as sources but not opened.
GA4GH DUO and dynamic-consent platforms for research are discovered as likely omissions, not primary-encoded.
ISO 27560 Annex F preference signals (including GPC) lack implementable primary detail here and are flagged not to be auto-promoted to consent.
Joint-controller, processor-chain and sub-processor grant graphs are only present as named_recipients, not as a full multi-party topology.
Death, incapacity and corporate succession have no single primary encoding.
Machine/AI agents as grantees are supported only insofar as ODRL Party and UMA client allow non-human parties; no primary standard defines AI-specific consent.
conflicts: Kantara Consent Receipt 1.1 is narrated as principal-to-controller; ISO/IEC TS 27560 receipt is organisation-to-principal.
ODRL Agreement can have a legal-person assigner; GDPR consent cannot.
FHIR grantee (must comply) is not identical to ODRL assignee (receives permission).
FHIR status vocabulary has no withdrawn code; DPV and GDPR treat withdrawal as first-class.
ODRL conflict strategy perm can prefer a Permission over a Prohibition, which collides with privacy fail-closed defaults.
ISO 27560 lawful_basis is optional on a consent record; GDPR always needs a basis.
UMA refresh must not re-assess authorization, so token lifetime can outrun a withdrawn grant unless explicitly revoked.
Kantara CR 1.1 field vocabulary is documented as not GDPR-aligned field-for-field.
FHIR Consent.action missing means all actions, while this catalogue's purpose is permission to read.
regional_assumptions: Privacy-flavour quality tests are written against GDPR as the densest primary privacy-consent statute; other regimes must be added as profiles.
Article 8 age of consent is a Member State value between 13 and 16; no single number is universal.
GDPR does not apply to deceased persons or to legal persons; those grants are usage-licence or local-law profiles.
ISO 27560 is a Technical Specification, not an IS; a revision (CD 27560.2) is in progress and may change mandatory fields.
FHIR Consent is Trial Use maturity 2; only the privacy use is fully modelled.
adversarial_checks: False permit: evaluating an ODRL Offer, a FHIR draft, or a Kantara receipt as if it were an active Agreement.
False permit: legal-person or public-authority 'consent' under power imbalance, or contract bundling of unnecessary processing.
False permit: child indication without parental capacity where Article 8 applies, or stale guardian after the child crosses the threshold.
False permit: purpose creep via Recital 50 compatibility language on a consent-based grant.
False permit: UMA refresh or cached validity token used after withdrawal because assessment is not re-run.
False deny: treating default-deny so naively that emergency or legal-obligation reads cannot be distinguished (those belong to other bases, not to this mixin).
Conformance theatre: asserting ISO 27560 or GDPR compliance because a JSON receipt exists, without indication evidence, unbundling or an integrity-protected master record.
Identifier collision: using consentTimestamp, FHIR date, or receipt id as the instrument primary key, splitting revocation.
Scope inflation: missing data_meaning treated as all data, or missing FHIR action treated as all actions, against this model's read-only purpose.
Propagation gap: status=withdrawn on the master while downstream processors still hold live RPTs.
